division.heading: Lawyers’ Charges, Retainer Agreements and Right of Review

operative_text.controlling:
10.15   The content of a retainer agreement, time records and other
evidence filed for the purposes of a review of a retainer agreement
or a lawyer’s charges is confidential and, unless otherwise ordered
by the Court,
(a) the court clerk, a review officer and any person under
their supervision must not disclose to any person the
information filed for the purposes of a review, and
(b) the copy of the information filed for the purposes of a
review is not available for inspection by any person other
than
(i) a party to the agreement,
(ii) a review officer, or
(iii) the Court.

BOOK_A.title: Retainer Agreement Conﬁdentiality
BOOK_A.commentary:
The winning party had a contingency agreement with their lawyer. The party having to pay
costs has an interest in the contingency agreement and is entitled to full disclosure of it. Rule
10.15(b) on conﬁdentiality does not apply. No one suggests the paying party is a party to the
agreement; the agreement becomes relevant by incorporation by reference in the costs award.¹

footnotes.text: Quite similar to previous R.617. R.617 was similar to R.617(4) ﬁrst enacted in 1994.
Barry v. Ind. Alliance Ins. (etc. ) (#2) 2022 ABKB 706, 52 Alta LR(7th) 706 (¶’s 8-12).

Read against the official text: the rule text equals official 10.15 (lead-in, (a), (b)(i)-(iii)); the bracket agrees with the official history (AR 124/2010; 140/2013; 36/2020) and with Book B ('Alta. Reg. 140/2013, s. 11; 36/2020, s. 12'). The note ('The winning party had a contingency agreement with their lawyer. The party having to pay costs has an interest in the contingency agreement and is entitled to full disclosure of it. Rule 10.15(b) on confidentiality does not apply. No one suggests the paying party is a party to the agreement; the agreement becomes relevant by incorporation by reference in the costs award.') is a summary of Barry v. Ind. Alliance Ins. (etc.) (#2) 2022 ABKB 706 (paras 8-12), not the text of the rule: official 10.15(b) lists who may inspect the copy ('a party to the agreement, a review officer, or the Court') and says nothing of a paying party, and 10.15 begins 'unless otherwise ordered by the Court'; the same paragraph is in the 10.5 note (p.10-13, line 569) and its authority is the same fn (fn 5 there); the note does not say that the disclosure was ordered by the Court under 10.15. History fn 5 (p.10-30): 'Quite similar to previous R.617. R.617 was similar to R.617(4) first enacted in 1994.' - the 10.14 history (1968 R.648) uses a different form and no 1968 year here; not corroborated by Book B or Book C, which print no history. supra/infra: no supra or infra is used in this note. Printed as is: 'Barry v. Ind. Alliance Ins. (etc. ) (#2)'.
